C-HZX-001E.category: 政治合法性理论/民本主义
C-HZX-001E.title_en: Tianxia as Principal, Ruler as Guest: Resetting Political Legitimacy in 'Origin of the Ruler'
C-HZX-001E.description_en: After the Ming's fall, Huang's 'Origin of the Ruler' traces rulership to a contracted role—cultivating public good and removing public harm—and condemns rulers who keep the realm as private estate as 'the great harm of Tianxia,' transferring the court of legitimacy from heaven's mandate to the lived welfare of all under heaven.

C-HZX-002E.category: 制度设计理论/治理方法论
C-HZX-002E.title_en: Good Law Before Good Men: The Institutional-Priority Manifesto of 'Origin of Law'
C-HZX-002E.description_en: 'Origin of Law' distinguishes the Three Dynasties' 'law of Tianxia' from the post-Qin 'law of one family,' arguing that 'non-law law' manacles the realm so even a worthy ruler cannot govern well—the order must invert: first establish public law, then seek the men.

C-HZX-003E.category: 公共领域理论/协商民主
C-HZX-003E.title_en: Public Right-and-Wrong Decided in Schools: The Grand Director's Vermilion-Inking
C-HZX-003E.description_en: The 'Schools' chapter designs an academic estate independent of the executive: the Grand Learning director ranks with the chancellor, decrees take effect only after public school deliberation and vermilion inking, and county schools review local governance each term—public reason given a statutory veto point.

C-HZX-004E.title_en: Li Is the Li of Qi: An Philosophical Audit Against 'Li Before Qi'
C-HZX-004E.description_en: Against Zhu Xi's 'li before qi,' Huang objects that a prior principle would be 'a separate thing'—the cosmos is one qi in flux and li is qi's own regularity. His calendrical science substantiates it: heaven's way is not an entity aloft but a computable process.

C-HZX-005E.title_en: One Essence, Many Manifestations: The Pluralist Academic History of the Ming Ru Xue An
C-HZX-005E.description_en: Compiling the 'Ming Ru Xue An,' Huang ruled that 'partial views and opposing arguments deserve a scholar's closest attention at their differences,' condemning the homogenization of 'pouring water into water'—schools stand side by side, and divergence itself becomes the information.

C-HZX-006E.title_en: Rooted in the Classics, Verified in the Histories: The Statecraft Pipeline of Learning
C-HZX-006E.description_en: 'Learning must be rooted in the classics to avoid treading on emptiness and verified in the histories to manage affairs'—Huang grounds scholarship in canonical norms, tests it against the historical record, and drags learning from late-Ming mind-nature talk back to the real battlefields of institutions, taxation, and defense.

C-HZX-007E.title_en: Astronomical Audit of the Classics: Recomputing the Spring-Autumn Eclipses
C-HZX-007E.description_en: Huang recomputed the thirty-six eclipses of the Spring and Autumn Annals with Han and Yuan calendar systems against the text, and his calendrical expertise fed the unmasking of the forged Old Text Documents—turning 'seeking truth from facts' into a falsification procedure with independent instruments.

C-HZX-008E.title_en: The Ratchet of Accumulated Harm: Huang Zongxi's Law of Fiscal Rebound
C-HZX-008E.description_en: The 'Land Tax' chapter tracks reform from the two-tax law to the Single Whip: each consolidation briefly lightens burdens, then new surcharges regrow beyond former levels—'accumulated harm cannot return,' the institutional logic by which tax merger without an anti-accretion lock guarantees rebound.

C-HZX-009E.category: 文化认同理论/民族政治学
C-HZX-009E.title_en: Distinguishing Yi and Xia by Civilization: The Leftover Subject's Standard
C-HZX-009E.description_en: After the Ming's fall Huang refused Qing office for life, grounding resistance in the Yi-Xia distinction—yet what he defended was culture, not blood: he accepted Western astronomy's precision and urged converging the two learnings, holding the civilizational standard above the political boundary while refusing to bless armed conquest.

C-HZX-010E.title_en: Synthesizing the Many into One: From Valley to River to Sea
C-HZX-010E.description_en: 'A scholar a thousand years on, unable to synthesize the many into one—from valley to river, river to sea—can this be called mastering the classics?' The 'Ming Ru Xue An' distills each school from its complete works, states each aim unreconciled, and lets the convergent structure of the many emerge from the material itself.
